tests.scope: Targeted building publication suite in isolated worktree; no full repository or hardware suite

limitations: Level-specific referenced plan geometry remains an approximate registered presentation; KG has separately registered geometry with assumed height
XY registration is uncalibrated; old L01 concept dimensions are assumptions, not measurements
Owner-assumed clear heights and illustrative slabs are not a surveyed structural model
Atrium proof covers floor-hole continuity only, excluding wall edges and the illustrative blue marker
No robot, route, physical clearance, load, egress or safety qualification; schematic wall-junction overlaps remain allowed
Circulation witnesses describe connected presentation geometry and scoped apertures, not walking, headroom, elevator operation or structural suitability
Roof, curved glass and guard dimensions are illustrative; no weather sealing, structural, fall-protection or fire-safety qualification
Cutaway/detail views change visibility only; no boolean cutaway is constructed; original photographs are not dependencies
EG uses a separately registered owner-labelled trace; OG1–OG3 reuse the canonical relative F03 template.
EG literals are manually aligned to referenced vertical cores, not photogrammetric or metric registration.
The XY ratio uses an unmeasured L01 parameter; it is a presentation proportion and does not calibrate F03.
Clear height is an owner assumption; slab thickness and source-referenced wall/door dimensions are presentation assumptions.
Actual EG floors cover the upper Atrium projection; no synthetic duplicate ground Atrium slab is added.
ConceptExchange is a semantic visual marker, not a selected lift, robot, rail, handover fixture or connecting trajectory.
Opening displays and constructive wall-junction overlaps retain the relative-floorplan limitations.
One internal right-hand staircase and a separate external metal fire staircase are shown; the building lift remains independent of both.

The X-axis glass cap covers Atrium, all source corridors and the explicitly selected inner core; only its perimeter skirt is facetted, with sagitta bounded relative to glass thickness. A local opaque external-stair access deck remains an explicit exception.
KG uses a separate manually registered trace; its clear height and floor pitch provisionally reuse the presentation assumptions, not a surveyed basement elevation.
KG facade details and exact stair geometry remain simplified; all XY coordinates are uncalibrated.
The foyer glass front and very open metal rails follow private owner photographs; their registration, grid and sizes remain illustrative.
Room door colour is owner-confirmed warm wood, approximated under photographic lighting. Door leaves are shown open; this is not a fire-door or egress state.
Earth at EG grade is an illustrative cutaway around the building, not a measured terrain survey.
Door-side roles are owner-confirmed; the opposite port is a stack-only concept override, not an observation added to the F03 trace.
Existing building lift and cabin are distinct from the blue Atrium future-exchange marker.
Cabin, shaft frame and two-flight stairs are static illustrative geometry, not selected equipment, normative stair design or an operating lift.
The inward EG port faces an unknown core region; no navigation or supported access beyond that port is asserted.
Deliberate connector/floor and rigid frame fusion contacts are construction assumptions, not load or safety qualification.
R3_017 is owner-confirmed as the external metal stair from EG to Roof; it is distinct from the internal R3_028 staircase and does not serve KG.
KG–EG is a static concept connector with assumed floor pitch; basement inward-only lift policy is modeled.

ground_floor.registration: manual shared-core anchoring, not rigid photogrammetry or metric calibration
